title: Turos Csusza
subtitle: Hungarian egg noodles with cottage cheese and crispy bacon
excerpt: Wide egg noodles tossed with silky cottage cheese and soured cream, then topped with crispy bacon and a spoonful of extra soured cream. A simple Hungarian comfort dish that comes together quickly.
sourceNotes: Classic Hungarian home cooking. Turos csusza is one of the most beloved everyday dishes in Hungary. Synthesised from multiple Hungarian culinary sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten straight away. The noodles absorb the cream as they sit.

content.text: Turos csusza is Hungary's answer to pasta with cheese. Wide noodles go with cottage cheese, soured cream, and fat, crispy strips of bacon. Do not drain the pasta too dry as a little cooking water helps the cheese melt into a loose sauce.
Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the tagliatelle according to the packet instructions until just tender.
While the pasta cooks, fry the streaky bacon in the dry frying pan over a medium-high heat for 8 minutes until crispy. Lift out with a slotted spoon and set aside. Leave the bacon fat in the pan.
Scoop out a cupful of pasta water before draining. Drain the pasta and return it to the large pan over a low heat.
Add the cottage cheese, half the soured cream, and 4 tablespoons of pasta water to the noodles. Toss well. The cheese should melt into the noodles rather than stay in chunks.
Add a splash more pasta water if the noodles look dry. Season with black pepper. Taste and add salt if needed.
Divide the noodles between four warm bowls. Spoon the remaining soured cream over the top.
Scatter the crispy bacon over each bowl. Serve straight away.

items.symptom: The cheese stays lumpy and does not melt in.
items.cause: The pasta was too cold, or the cheese was straight from the fridge.
items.fix: Use hot pasta and take the cottage cheese out of the fridge 15 minutes before cooking. Toss vigorously over a low heat.

items.symptom: The dish is dry and stodgy.
items.cause: Not enough pasta water was added.
items.fix: Add pasta water a tablespoon at a time until the noodles are loose and coated.

items.symptom: The bacon is chewy rather than crispy.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough, or the bacon was added in too large a batch.
items.fix: Fry in a single layer in a dry pan on a medium-high heat. Do not move the pieces until they begin to colour.
